correctness.rationale: For any k, choose complements to ker D and bases of im D. The bracket of inputs (a_i,v_i),(a_h,v_h) has coordinates a_i Dv_h−a_h Dv_i in im D. This identifies defining ideals under a linear input change, with c independent kernel coordinates per input; it is not merely a pointwise match. If a is nonzero, every row of Y is a multiple of a, so the support is the union of a=0 and the rank-at-most-one stacked matrix locus. The irreducible rank-one cone has dimension equal to number of rows plus number of columns minus one, and neither locus contains the other for r,s≥2. This proves the stated dimensions, intersection and unique equidimensional case. For finite fields, counting on a=0 and a≠0 gives N_s and hence the displayed zeta function. On all tuples the joint map is (b,u)↦(a_i u−b y_i)_i: when a=0 it has rank 0 or 1; otherwise the u-block has rank r and the b-column adds one precisely when Y is not of the form ua. This gives the claimed four frequencies, including in characteristic 2. For the nilpotent rank-two example D_{31}²≠0 and D_{22}²=0; γ_{j+1}=D^jV, and the central quotient is abelian exactly when D²=0. For d≤3, rank fixes the nilpotent partition. Independent direct simultaneous-centralizer enumeration used two invertible rank-two matrices over F₂ and one rank-two singular matrix over F₃, checking both the rank frequencies and commuting counts (python3 /workspace/reviews/evidence/reproduce.py 1).
residual_risks: The agreement for the nilpotent examples is not an assertion about arbitrary pairs of Lie algebras. Component claims in the frozen statement concern reduced geometric support. The finite reproducibility check is not a scheme proof.

evidence: Rauh's general decomposition gives exactly the full vertex set and the set of all leaves for K_{1,r}. The first is connected, so all columns are proportional; the other kills a and leaves isolated columns unconstrained. Rauh's radicality result even strengthens the geometric-support formulation.
Goodwin–Röhrle give two commuting-pair components in the B₂ nilradical; Richardson treats reductive commuting varieties and notes solvable reducibility.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader graph theorem gives the whole component geometry mechanically, and point counts follow readily from the model. It does not enumerate joint centralizers in the Lie category or exhibit the nilpotent collision.

evidence: The graph primary decomposition applies once the equations are identified. It says nothing about shifting inputs between Lie algebras without respecting the central quotient bracket.
The explicit central quotients in the frozen example do not even agree in abelianness, so prior sufficient results for isoclinic Lie algebras would not explain this collision.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Distinguish linear input/output equivalence of the alternating bracket maps from isomorphism of central quotient Lie algebras. The concrete consequence at the first possible dimension and the Lie joint-adjoint polynomial are not just the graph component theorem.

originality.rationale: The common ideal is exactly a known generalized binomial edge ideal after transpose, and its decomposition and the component formulas are covered. Credit that prior result rather than treating the geometry of this model as new. The distinct contribution is the Lie-theoretic identification of all-arity commuting schemes and joint-adjoint rank distributions for same-dimension, same-rank almost-abelian algebras, including the sharp nonisoclinic class-two/class-three collision. No checked source covers that conclusion or the full joint-adjoint enumerator.
residual_risks: One broad public search was nonresponsive and the isoclinism paper's full text was unavailable. A specialized Lie bracket-map or joint-centralizer result might cover additional parts; a search miss is not proof.

value.rationale: The value is the sharp failure of Lie reconstruction even if every ordered-tuple commuting scheme and every joint-adjoint rank frequency is supplied. The pair changes nilpotency class and isoclinism at the first possible dimension, so it isolates a real loss of structure. The known determinantal component geometry alone is not the value claim.
